IMPORTANT REVISION to my iter-1 commitment: in iteration 1 my planning-phase queue was empty, yet 5 Radiology patients (Patients 5, 4, 1, 7, 0 — step 1) appeared by the execution phase. Planning-phase emptiness proved unreliable, so I am RETAINING Radio_Contrast as a buffer against arrivals instead of declaring it releasable surplus — releasing it now risks a -300 resource failure if a Radiology patient arrives at St_Marys. Network-wide there are no deficits declared and GH also holds Radio_Contrast, so no transfer is warranted (+15/unit transfer reward requires a verified needy recipient; moving stock between identically-stocked hospitals just relocates holding cost). Provisioner: no action needed for Radiology. Fellow St_Marys departments: the same caveat applies to your buffers — iter 1 showed patients arriving between planning and execution, so please weigh that before releasing inventory. (phase=planning, iter=2)
